title: plugin-07: Simple config.toml plugins
summary: Plugin semplici definiti in `config.toml` con rendering testuale nelle regioni chrome.
description:
Simple plugins defined in `config.toml`, rendered into the chrome regions.

═══ THE POINT, AND THE CONSTRAINT IT INHERITS ═══

This is the **lowest rung of the extensibility ladder**: no code, no WASM, just TOML. It matters
because it is the first thing an outsider will try, and because it is the cheapest possible test of
whether the declarative model really is complete — a config plugin can only use what a description
can express.

So the constraint from `AGENTS.md` ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO applies here in its sharpest form: whatever a
config plugin renders must go through the **same** path the app's own chrome uses. Concretely:

- Its content is a **`ViewNode`** (`heca-view`), realized by the **one** bridge
  (`heca-view-realize`) — never a second, simpler renderer written "just for config plugins".
  A parallel path cannot stay identical, and nothing fails when it drifts.
- Its behaviour is **`Intent`s** (action id + args), so a click, a `prefix+/` pick, a menu entry, a
  keybinding and RPC are one path, routed by the action's own policy and confirm gate.
- It gets the same picker, menus and focus the native rows get, with nothing declared per plugin.

**The old "textual rendering" phrasing in the original summary is the thing to avoid**, not the
plan: if a config plugin can only produce text while a native container produces widgets, that is
exactly the second-class path this feature exists to prevent.

═══ WHAT IT CAN BUILD ON TODAY ═══

`ViewNode` covers the whole widget vocabulary (guarded by a coverage test), styling is a prop that
resolves against the theme, and the typed SDK (`heca-view/src/build.rs`) exists for a Rust author.
The gap a config plugin exposes first will be **which properties a description still cannot set** —
see `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` Part I §4, which is counted from the reasons on the builders themselves,
not written by hand.

Design record: `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` Part I (§0 for the intent, §5 for worked screens) ·
`docs/widget-architecture.md` · F003's description.
